title: RAW UNREVIEWED: Frontinus separates fixed aperture from head-dependent and orientation-dependent delivery
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. Frontinus links delivery to height and route, then contrasts intake orientations; the bronze calix fixes the granted opening against easy alteration. A fixed opening and a delivery quantity are distinct. Relative head/path and intake alignment change the delivery comparison, while material rigidity resists tampering with the aperture. The same conduit can keep its licensed opening while differing in delivered flow.

source.span: De aquaeductu 35-36, complete chapters; the calix construction and grant condition in 36.3-5 are mandatory

design.mechanism: A fixed opening and a delivery quantity are distinct. Relative head/path and intake alignment change the delivery comparison, while material rigidity resists tampering with the aperture. The same conduit can keep its licensed opening while differing in delivered flow.
design.unit: Complete chapters 35-36 and a future complete admitted connected-vessel passage with owned intake, direction and fixed-size conditions.
design.contrast: Diameter-only delivery makes every same-aperture case equal. Direction-only flow loses the grant and rigid-fitting role. A universal conservation claim confuses measured delivery with a fixed upstream quantity the source has not supplied.
design.prediction: Preserve aperture identity across the orientation contrast, bind more/less delivery to that opening, and keep the tamper-resistant material statement separate from a physical flow law. No modern pressure equation, Reynolds number or numeral gloss follows.
design.scope: Raw source relation only; no chosen manuscript words, image inspection or semantic experiment
